'''''Jasminum multipartitum''''', the '''starry wild jasmine''', '''African jasmine''', or '''imfohlafohlane''', is a species of [[jasmine]], in the family [[Oleaceae]], that is native to [[Southern Africa]].<ref name="sarahduke">[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=351553 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families, ''Jasminum multipartitum'']</ref>

==Description==
This {{convert|3|m|ft|adj=mid|-tall}} scrambling climber, that can also be grown as a {{convert|1.5|m|ft|adj=mid|-tall}} shrub, thrives in the sun or semi-shade. It produces masses of white, scented, star-shaped flowers and it attracts a variety of birds.<ref>Hochstetter, Christian Ferdinand Friedrich. 1844. Flora; oder, (allgemeine) botanische Zeitung. Regensburg, Jena, ''Jasminum multipartitum''</ref> It flowers from late spring to summer.
[[File:Starr 980529-1414 Jasminum multipartitum.jpg|thumb|Leaves]]
==Distribution==
This is one of approximately ten species of Jasmine that occur in South Africa. Native to [[Mozambique]], [[Zimbabwe]], [[Eswatini]] and [[South Africa]], ''Starry Wild Jasmine'' is naturally found in the woodlands of the [[Eastern Cape]] and [[Kwazulu Natal]], as well as inland as far as [[Johannesburg]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.plantzafrica.com/planthij/jasminmulti.htm |title=Jasminum multipartitum |access-date=2011-01-31 |archive-date=2012-10-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121031033609/http://www.plantzafrica.com/planthij/jasminmulti.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Etymology==
'Jasminum' is a [[Latin]]ized form of the [[Persian language|Persian]] word, 'yasemin' for sweetly scented plants.<ref name="gledhill">Gledhill, David (2008). "The Names of Plants". Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9780521866453}} (hardback), {{ISBN|9780521685535}} (paperback).  pp 220</ref>
 
Latin species name ''multipartitus'' means divided into several or many parts, referring to the shape of the flower; it comes from ''multi-'' + ''partitus'', past participle of ''partire'' 'to divide', from ''part-'', ''pars'' 'part'.
